Since you're still on nicotine, I'll give you some tips that helped me quit.

The cravings come in cycles and will only last for several minutes at a time. IIRC, and I may not be, it's something like 2-5 minutes, and possibly up to 7 minutes at most. If you can last through that short initial time period, you should be good for a longer period after it.

The next thing is that the longer you go without nicotine, the less severe and less frequent the cravings will be. So as bad as it may be now, as long as you can stay off, it will only get easier. Reminding myself of that was very helpful. I knew that the suffering I was enduring at the moment was worth it, because I was buying myself an easier future with that suffering. If I could go one month, I could go 2, and the second month would be easier, and if I could go 2 months, then 3 would be even easier, and 6 would be even easier than that, and so on and so forth until I eventually would hardly think of smoking at all.

The next thing I did was create a tangible physical manifestation of my desire to quit. It was something that I could not simply get rid of easily. Something I could see and would have to confront every day if I failed, that would always remind me of that failure if I gave up. This helped me to stay strong and not give in, because I knew I didn't want to always be confronted with a representation of my own failure.

The last thing I did was substitute the sensation of smoking with the sensation of hot liquid hitting the back of my throat. For this, I used either decaffeinated or normal green tea, peppermint tea, or plain hot water.

Those were some of the main things that helped me quit smoking cold turkey after so many previously failed attempts.

If you want something badly enough, as long as that thing is possible, then you will always find a way to make it happen.
